summary: Deployed inventory-api as an OOM-protected systemd service on node1 (RHEL 7.9) and proved, with a live kernel OOM event, that it keeps serving while the kernel kills the memory-hog process. Then completed the mandatory single-node restart/evidence protocol.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 7.9, 2GB RAM/2GB swap, systemd 219, python2 only, firewalld active).

Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py (python2 HTTP JSON API on :8080 with /health) and installed it as inventory-api.service with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, Restart=always, enabled+started; verified serving via curl.
Wrote /opt/memory-hog/hog.py (unbounded memory allocator) and installed as memory-hog.service with default high OOMScoreAdjust=900, Restart=no; opened firewalld port 8080.
Captured pre-test baseline: inventory-api active, MainPID oom_score_adj=-1000.
Disabled swap (swapoff -a) to force a deterministic system-wide OOM condition, started memory-hog.service, polled memory usage.
Kernel oom-killer fired and killed PID 2031 (memory-hog, oom_score_adj=900); confirmed via dmesg 'Killed process 2031 (python2)...' and memory-hog.service entering failed/signal=KILL state.
Confirmed inventory-api.service remained continuously active (same start timestamp/PID, no restart) and still answered /health and / after the OOM kill; restored swap (swapon -a).
Reset failed memory-hog unit, captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline.
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 via backgrounded nohup so the ack returned before disconnect; polled until SSH/exec was available again.
Verified new boot_id differs from baseline, confirmed inventory-api auto-started on boot (enabled, active, oom_score_adj=-1000) and is serving again, and swap is restored to its original state.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (systemd) service and actively serving
evidence.summary: systemctl start/is-active=active and curl /health, / return valid JSON immediately after unit creation.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api protected from OOM killer via oom_score_adj
evidence.summary: Main PID's /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj reads -1000, sourced from OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 in the unit.

evidence.requirement: System driven out of memory by a memory-hungry process
evidence.summary: Swap disabled, memory-hog.service started (oom_score_adj=900) and memory usage climbs toward exhaustion (779M used and rising).

evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM-killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: dmesg shows 'python2 invoked oom-killer... oom_score_adj=900' and 'Killed process 2031 (python2)' matching the hog's PID; free -h shows memory reclaimed.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving through and after the OOM event
evidence.summary: memory-hog.service shows failed/signal=KILL while inventory-api.service shows uninterrupted Active since original start time; curl /health and / succeed post-kill.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 325732f1-... plus inventory-api enabled/active and a working /health call before rebooting.
Backgrounded systemctl reboot command returns its ack (connection then drops), confirming the reboot was issued non-blockingly.

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Poll sequence shows connection down then recovering; new boot_id d91b039b-4acf-4baa-8deb-f26f4d15bd22 differs from the pre-restart baseline, and fresh uptime confirms a real reboot.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of inventory-api and system state
evidence.summary: inventory-api.service auto-started (enabled), active with fresh PID, oom_score_adj=-1000 intact, /health and / respond correctly, and swap is restored to its original 2GB configuration.
